methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective single-institution cohort of 659 EC patients spanning 1989-2022, which raises concerns about treatment-era heterogeneity not addressed in analysis. The AI classifier was trained on only 2235 lymphocytes from 4 cases and tested on 2 cases — a very small training/validation base that the authors themselves flag as a limitation. The ROC-derived cut-off (AUC 0.570, barely above chance) was defined and applied in the same dataset without an independent cohort, risking optimistic bias; a prespecified cut-off or split-sample design would have strengthened inference. Cox models used backward selection without reported handling of missing data or multiplicity correction across multiple subgroup analyses (histology, MMR); sensitivity analyses with alternative cut-offs and the interaction term for MMR are credits. No power calculation is reported and inter-observer reproducibility of the manual frontline annotation — a key upstream input — was not assessed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Design is an individual retrospective cohort study with survival endpoints at a single center, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Endpoints (PFS, OS) are patient-relevant, and the question — standardized, reproducible TIL quantification in EC — is clinically meaningful given existing literature on TIL prognostic value and emerging immunotherapy indications in dMMR/MSI-H EC. However, the discriminative performance of the model is modest (AUC 0.570), it is not integrated with molecular classification (POLE untested, TMB not assessed), and no external validation or decision-curve analysis supports clinical utility. The translational path is plausible but requires substantial additional validation before informing practice.

reporting_quality.justification: As a biomarker/prognostic study, REMARK is the appropriate checklist. The manuscript reports patient selection, assay details (HALO/Object Phenotyper, F1 score, antibody clones/dilutions, cut-off derivation), univariate/multivariate Cox models, and a detailed limitations section — covering many REMARK items. Gaps include no flow diagram of included/excluded patients, no explicit prespecified analysis plan, limited reporting of missing data handling, and no reporting of inter-observer reproducibility for the manual annotation step. Data and code availability are not described in the blinded text; the AI classifier, trained weights, and whole-slide images are not stated as publicly available, and no repository identifiers are provided — reproducibility is limited to protocol description.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical/methodological: applying an AI-based (HALO Object Phenotyper) lymphocyte quantification pipeline centered on the invasive frontline specifically to EC, where prior AI-TIL work has focused on breast, colorectal, esophageal, and ovarian (ref 23) cancers. TIL prognostic significance in EC with manual scoring is already well established (refs 13–16, 31–34), and the authors themselves (ref 15) have reported manual TIL-based prognostic models in EC, making this a meaningful but incremental extension. The approach does not introduce a new deep-learning architecture or a new biological concept, and the method remains tied to proprietary commercial software rather than a novel algorithm. Positioning is reasonable and does not over-claim 'first-in-class' status.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a clear IMRaD structure, abbreviations expanded on first use, and figure captions that are informative and self-contained. The abstract is quantitatively grounded and accurately reflects the main findings. Weaknesses include a very long single-paragraph limitations section at the end of the Discussion that bundles numerous distinct caveats, some redundancy between Results and Discussion (e.g., F1 score discussed twice), and inconsistency between the reported ROC AUC in Results (0.570) and the Figure 4 caption (0.573). The Discussion is heavy on reiteration and comparatively light on mechanistic or clinical interpretation of the modest AUC.

key_strengths: Large single-center cohort (n=659) with long follow-up (median 63 months) and standardized restaging to 2023 FIGO criteria
Clear operational definition of the evaluation region (500 μm span across the invasive frontline) with exploratory comparison of alternative regions
Multivariate Cox analysis plus prespecified subgroup analyses by histology and MMR status, with an MMR×TIL interaction term
Thorough and candid limitations section acknowledging small AI training base, lack of external validation, and absence of POLE testing
key_concerns: Discriminative performance is weak (ROC AUC 0.570) and the cut-off was derived and applied in the same dataset, with no external or split-sample validation
AI classifier trained on only 2235 lymphocytes from 4 cases with 2-case F1 testing; histological subtype not considered in training set
Single-center retrospective design spanning 33 years (1989–2022) without analysis of treatment-era effects or inter-observer reproducibility of the manual frontline annotation
No data/code availability statement; proprietary commercial software (HALO) limits reproducibility, and no molecular integration (POLE, TMB) is attempted
Minor numerical inconsistency between text AUC (0.570) and Figure 4 caption (0.573); multiplicity across numerous subgroup/sensitivity analyses is not corrected
Novelty is incremental — AI-based TIL quantification has been reported in several other cancers including a closely analogous ovarian HGSC pipeline (ref 23)
chief_reviewer.rationale: The manuscript is a competently executed but incremental retrospective biomarker study with modest discrimination and no external validation, limiting it to a lower-tier oncology journal where it can serve as a hypothesis-generating contribution after addressing reporting gaps and the AUC inconsistency.
